item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 301134
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on recently
upgraded Hurricane Karina, located well west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Tropical
Storm Lowell, located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of disturbed weather, associated with a tropical wave, is
located well to the south of southwestern Mexico. This system is
expected to continue to move west-northwestward to northwestward at
10 to 15 mph. Environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual
development of this system, and a tropical depression is likely to
form during the early to middle part of next week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in the next couple of days. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while it moves slowly westward
across the central Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Hurricane Karina Public Advisory Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 301448
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Karina Advisory Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
800 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026
 
...KARINA EXPECTED TO BECOME STRONGER AS IT MOVES OVER THE OPEN
PACIFIC OCEAN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.3N 122.1W
ABOUT 880 MI...1415 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...80 MPH...130 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...980 MB...28.94 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located
near latitude 17.3 North, longitude 122.1 West. Karina is moving
toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A slower westward
to west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 80 mph (130 km/h) with higher
gusts. Steady to rapid strengthening seems likely, and Karina is
forecast to become a major hurricane in a day or so.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles
(370 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 980 mb (28.94 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Karina will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
couple of days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening
surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your
local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 301449
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
800 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026
 
The most recent satellite images show that Karina is undergoing 
some structural changes in the inner core as a new burst of 
convection has developed on the southwestern portion of the 
cyclone. The most recent TAFB Dvorak intensity estimate remains 
T4.0/65 kt, and the most recent objective satellite estimates are 
in the range of 61-80 kt. Thus, the initial intensity for this 
advisory remains at 70 kt. 

The cyclone has a good fundamental inner core structure and a 
favorable environment, thus Karina should be strengthening for the 
next day or two day. It will be around this time that Karina could 
reach major hurricane status. However, the environmental conditions 
will start to become less favorable later Monday, at which the 
intensification process should come to a halt. As the environment 
becomes more hostile, due to the progressively cooler waters and 
drier air, the hurricane should start to weaken during the middle 
and later parts of the week. The current NHC intensity forecast is 
on the higher end of the guidance, but still below the GDMI and the 
HCCA aids. 
 
The hurricane is moving west-northwestward at about 11 kt. The high
pressure system to the north of Karina is expected to weaken due to
an amplifying trough over the western U.S. However, there should be
enough ridging to keep Karina on a westward to west-northwestward
course. There is still a good amount of spread in the track models 
days 3 and beyond at this time, so there is a higher degree of 
uncertainty in how far north the cyclone will move. The current 
NHC track is a bit further south of the previous track, but still 
remains on the northern side of the guidance envelope.
